title: Effort and the gem
literal_meaning: If one makes an effort, one finds a gem.
explanation: The small change from jatna, effort, to ratna, gem, gives the line its compact promise. The valuable result is pictured as something worth looking and working for. A speaker can use the conditional line to encourage another attempt when a task seems unrewarding. This encouraging use follows the wording and the dictionary definition of trying; it is not evidence that effort always succeeds. In our reading, the gem gives effort a direction without making failure a verdict on someone’s worth.
meaning_odia: ଯତ୍ନରୁ ରତ୍ନ—ଧ୍ୱନିର ଛୋଟ ବଦଳରେ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଓ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଫଳ ପାଖାପାଖି ଆସିଯାଏ। ଖୋଜିବା ଓ କାମ କରିବାର ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ରତ୍ନର ଚିତ୍ର ଟାଣେ। କୌଣସି କାମରେ ଫଳ ନ ଦେଖି ମନ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଆଉଥରେ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରିବାକୁ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ଉତ୍ସାହର କଥା; ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ସଫଳତା ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ବା ଅସଫଳ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କମ୍ ବୋଲି ବିଚାର ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: The rhyme encourages effort toward a worthwhile result, without guaranteeing success.
odia_summary: ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ରତ୍ନର ମିଳ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଫଳ ପାଇଁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାର ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦିଏ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends are trying to mend a loose chair. After the first adjustment fails, one says “ଯତ୍ନ କଲେ ରତ୍ନ ମିଳେ” and suggests checking the other joint. The line encourages a more careful second attempt rather than promising that the chair must be repairable.
cultural_context: Source definesଯତ୍ନ କରିବା as trying/endeavouring and labels the lineଢଗ. Sound contrast and encouragement are editorial close reading, not a named author’s theory or origin account.
